references.name: Peter Temin

references.name: Gabriel Kolko
references.desc: The Triumph of Conservatism — Progressive-era reforms as big-business cartelization

references.name: William Gouge
references.desc: Jacksonian monetary theorist; "The Bank was saved, and the people were ruined"

references.name: Condy Raguet
references.desc: Philadelphia senator who explained to David Ricardo why banks couldn't be disciplined: the entire population was either stockholders or debtors

references.name: Charles A. Conant
references.desc: A History of Modern Banks of Issue (1896), The Principles of Money and Banking (1905) — surplus-capital theory, monetary imperialism, gold-exchange standard architect

references.name: Irving Fisher
references.desc: Yale economist; price stabilization, Stable Money League, proto-monetarism; personally ruined by the 1929 crash

references.name: H. Parker Willis
references.desc: Columbia professor; drafted the Federal Reserve Act with Carter Glass; later became the Fed's fiercest qualitative critic

references.name: J. Laurence Laughlin
references.desc: University of Chicago economist; directed both the Indianapolis Monetary Commission and the National Citizens' League for Sound Banking

references.name: Paul Moritz Warburg
references.desc: Kuhn, Loeb partner; chief architect of the Federal Reserve's structure and the acceptance market; chairman of International Acceptance Bank

references.name: Benjamin M. Anderson
references.desc: Chase National Bank chief economist; leading hard-money critic of Fed inflationism in the 1920s–30s

references.name: Ralph Hawtrey
references.desc: British Treasury official; major theoretical architect of the gold-exchange standard and price-level stabilization

references.name: John Maynard Keynes
references.desc: Indian Currency and Finance (1913) — first champion of the gold-exchange standard; Keynes Plan for Bretton Woods (bancor)

references.name: Edwin W. Kemmerer
references.desc: Princeton economist; imposed central banks and gold-exchange standards on Third World countries while collecting fees from Dillon, Read

references.name: Marriner Eccles
references.desc: Western banker; proto-Keynesian who shifted Fed power from NY Fed to Washington via the Banking Act of 1935

references.name: Lauchlin Currie
references.desc: Harvard monetarist; Eccles's key aide who drafted the Banking Act of 1935 provisions centralizing Fed control

references.name: Jacques Rueff
references.desc: French economist; advocate for return to classical gold standard; influenced de Gaulle's monetary policy

references.name: Emile Moreau
references.desc: Bank of France governor; exposed British monetary imperialism through the gold-exchange standard

references.name: E.R.A. Seligman
references.desc: Columbia economist; organized conferences promoting central banking; hailed economists as society's philosopher-kings

references.name: George F. Warren
references.desc: Cornell agricultural economist; inspired FDR's gold-price manipulation program

references.name: Foster & Catchings
references.desc: Underconsumptionist economists whose theories influenced both Hoover and Eccles
